sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The latest arXiv cycle surfaced production-scale agent engineering from Meta and an Anthropic safety study on prompt-conditioned false beliefs. Meta's papers report operational gains, while the Anthropic work explores a scalable way to construct model organisms and warns that training interventions can undermine evaluation reliability.

sections.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
attribution_evidence: Meta author affiliations listed in the arXiv record
sections.problem: Fixed inference dispatch rates become miscalibrated as fleet capacity and request lengths change, creating idle capacity or excess queues.
sections.method: A per-replica admission cap rejects work before long waits; a stateful dispatcher uses capacity refusals to probe and track the live ceiling, with durable priority queues for retries.
sections.key_result: In a same-traffic production A/B, the shaper served a classifier using 43% fewer H100s than its queued, fixed-rate predecessor. In steady-capacity replay, throughput was within 1% of an aggressively tuned fixed rate with roughly one-quarter its refusal share.
sections.caveat: Lower-priority work waited longer at backfill peaks; the replay and the production A/B are different evaluations, and the headline resource saving is workload-specific.
sections.why_it_matters: This is evidence that adaptive admission control can improve real inference utilization at large scale without relying on output-length forecasts or fleet-wide rate retuning.

sections.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
attribution_evidence: Meta Platforms affiliations listed for the authors
sections.problem: Search-ranking improvements require slow cycles of coding, training, and evaluation; offline metrics may not predict online impact.
sections.method: Human-on-the-loop agents propose code changes, launch training, inspect offline results, and decide which candidates merit review. The system uses parallel experiments and an objective calibrated against online outcomes.
sections.key_result: In one campaign, 325 of 1,097 completed candidates were accepted (29.6%); the best model increased search volume by 0.23% in a large-scale A/B test.
sections.caveat: The 29.6% acceptance rate is compared with an earlier campaign that used a different objective and search constraint; the online lift is modest and specific to the reported ranking system.
sections.why_it_matters: It moves agentic ML engineering from benchmark tasks into a live industrial recommender workflow, while retaining human control over objectives and final review.

sections.title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
attribution_evidence: Anthropic and Anthropic Fellows Program author affiliations listed in the arXiv record
sections.problem: Synthetic-document fine-tuning can implant false beliefs, but traditionally requires separate training for each injected fact, limiting scale for alignment evaluations.
sections.method: Prompt-conditioned synthetic-document fine-tuning trains one model on documents conditioned on facts supplied in a prompt; the authors assess belief depth on held-out facts and test a subsequent RL intervention.
sections.key_result: Belief depth on unseen facts scales roughly log-linearly with the number of training facts. RL that reduces verbal compliance with false prompt facts generalizes to held-out evaluations and approaches SDF on some measures.
sections.caveat: Initial alignment-audit experiments were negative on the small models studied, and optimizing one belief-depth metric made that evaluation less trustworthy.
sections.why_it_matters: The work offers a potentially cheaper way to construct model organisms for alignment research, while showing that the measurement procedure itself can be affected by training.

sections.title: Research Themes
content: Production agent systems are increasingly built around feedback and live constraints: Meta's MLE agents iterate over model changes, while Cap-and-Track steers inference dispatch using observed capacity refusals.

More capable or controllable agent behavior creates an oversight burden: Meta keeps engineers in the loop for consequential model changes, while Anthropic finds that prompt-conditioned training can alter both model beliefs and the reliability of evaluation signals.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest operational signal is Meta's use of agents and adaptive control inside production recommendation and inference systems, with measurable but workload-specific efficiency gains. The safety result is a reminder that evaluation quality must be checked alongside capability: training designed to shape behavior can also undermine the metrics used to assess it.
